prompt: I need to recall what we decided about the database migration strategy
expected_output: The agent should scan and read stored wiki knowledge about the database migration strategy.
assertions: Agent lists or searches wiki entries before reading any of them
Agent does not attempt to create or edit any entry
Agent presents found results or clearly states nothing was found

prompt: Remember that we decided to use Redis for session storage because of its low latency
expected_output: The agent should check for duplicates, then create a new wiki entry capturing the Redis session storage decision.
assertions: Agent lists existing entries before creating a new one
Agent calls wikictl create with a kebab-case, topic-based name
The entry body includes the rationale about low latency

prompt: Save a note about our API rate limiting: we use 100 requests per minute per user
expected_output: The agent should create an entry with a kebab-case name like 'api-rate-limiting'.
assertions: Agent generates a kebab-case entry name with no spaces, uppercase letters, or special characters
The entry body captures the rate limit details (100 req/min/user)
Agent passes 2-4 tags drawn from the shared tag vocabulary

prompt: Update the description of the 'api-rate-limiting' entry to mention we increased the limit to 200 requests per minute
expected_output: The agent should edit only the description field of the existing api-rate-limiting entry.
assertions: Agent finds the existing entry before editing (does not create a duplicate)
Agent updates only the description, leaving tags and body untouched
The updated description mentions 200 requests per minute

prompt: Add a section about error handling to the existing 'api-design-guidelines' entry, keep everything else
expected_output: The agent should append the error handling section to the existing body without dropping current content.
assertions: Agent reads the current entry body first, since --body/body replaces rather than appends
Agent preserves all existing content in the new body it writes
Agent appends the new error handling section to the body

prompt: How do our caching strategy and database indexing decisions relate to each other?
expected_output: The agent should retrieve entries about both caching and database indexing, then correlate the information.
assertions: Agent scans metadata (list or search) covering both topics before reading anything
Agent reads the full content of the entries it judged relevant
Agent synthesizes information from multiple entries, flagging any contradiction instead of silently picking one

prompt: Update the note about logging conventions, or create it if it doesn't exist yet
expected_output: The agent should check whether the entry exists, then edit if found or create if not.
assertions: Agent checks for an existing logging-conventions entry before acting
If found, agent edits it instead of creating a duplicate
If not found, agent creates a new entry

prompt: An MCP client is connected to the wikictl server — find what we know about deployment and summarize it
expected_output: The agent should use the wikictl MCP tools (list_entries/read_entry) instead of the CLI, following the same scan-then-read workflow.
assertions: Agent calls list_entries (optionally with a tag) before read_entry
Agent calls read_entry only for entries judged relevant from the list_entries metadata
Agent does not fall back to the CLI when an MCP client is available
